answer: Fork-evident sealed-counter attestation: each agent identity is a signing key sealed to a unique TPM/PUF and a monotonic counter. Every pulse, a coordinator sends a random tundra nonce; the agent signs it with the next counter value into a public onyx log. A copied key used by two live agents advances the same counter into divergent signed records, publicly exposing the fork. Cost: an attacker must provision distinct secure hardware per sybil identity and cannot clone keys without detectable equivocation.
